6a226c484b54f546d8876723.title: The Role of Waste in Sustainable Development
6a226c484b54f546d8876723.subtitle: The benefits of managing our waste properly
6a226c484b54f546d8876723.body:
Every day, humans discard an enormous amount of waste generated by countless activities. We can see this everywhere: in homes, schools, hospitals, shops, industries, on the street, and so on. Where does all that waste end up? Where do you think the first plastic bottle you ever used is now? Perhaps it was recycled, but it is more likely sitting in a landfill, where it will stay for hundreds of years.

In Mexico we generate 102,895 tons of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) every day, and 78.54% of it ends up in an open-air dump: a form of final disposal in which waste is placed on the ground with no kind of management, which makes it highly polluting. Another 9.63% of the waste is recycled, and the remainder is not collected (Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, 2017).

Managing our waste properly is essential if we want to talk about a sustainable future. We should not treat our waste as garbage: many of the materials we throw away can have another use and be brought back into the value chain instead of being sent to final disposal. This recovery of waste can happen in different ways, such as recycling, reuse, and returning materials to the soil; in addition, we should try to use as few materials as possible in the first place.

There are many types of waste, and they can be classified in several ways: organic, inorganic, plastics, metals, glass, wood, textiles, electronic waste, and so on. Separating this waste is extremely important because each type must go through a different process to be recycled, since they all have different characteristics. Separating waste also encourages the creation of markets for recyclable materials, reduces the volume of waste, and helps curb the degradation of natural resources (García, n.d.).

The benefits of managing our waste properly are very significant: we reduce the greenhouse gas emissions released in landfills by the decomposition of garbage, we extract fewer natural resources because we use the materials we already have, we save a great deal of energy and water, and we reduce pollution, among other things (INCINEROX, 2021).

Besides these environmental benefits, good waste treatment also brings economic and social advantages. On the economic side, it is an engine for creating new jobs; it also lowers operating costs for companies by using waste instead of virgin raw materials. On the social side, we can see the creation of new jobs, a decrease in the spread of disease, and a cleaner environment (Hernández, 2018).

As we have seen, managing our waste properly has many positive effects. It is one of the many essential steps we must take to be able to talk about a sustainable future, a livable planet, and a dignified life.

6a226c484b54f546d8876725.title: Harnessing Waste to Generate Energy
6a226c484b54f546d8876725.subtitle: Producing electricity from waste
6a226c484b54f546d8876725.body:
Electricity generation in Mexico falls into 7 categories: natural gas, coal, nuclear, hydroelectric, wind and solar, biomass, and oil. Most of it is produced from natural gas. As the International Energy Agency notes, the global trend is toward producing energy through these same methods, although others are also included, such as geothermal generation. The energy transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is a challenge for humanity, because it means breaking away from conventional ways of doing things. Even so, technologies are being developed more and more, both conventional ones and especially renewable ones.



For the energy transition, it is not realistic to rely on technologies entirely outside fossil-fuel-based processes. For this reason, strategies for producing energy are being sought that build on the foundations of fossil-fuel energy, using sources such as nuclear fission, biogas, or solar collectors, so that conventional generation technologies can run on sources with a lower environmental impact. According to Dr. González Santaló, the technology that would make the most sense is to keep using combined-cycle plants for power generation, since their high efficiency and low cost compared with the other processes reviewed indicate that, for a more efficient use of the calorific value of fossil fuels, combined cycle remains the best option. The approach changes, however, if one starts from the idea of using renewable fuels
(biomass) and gasifying them in order to generate
electricity from that resource.



Gasification is a thermochemical process that converts solid biomass into a combustible gas under high-temperature conditions and in the presence of a gasifying agent (air, oxygen, steam, etc.). The result is a fuel with a calorific value similar to natural gas, coming from clean sources. Ultimately, these processes become a real alternative to fossil fuels, since they can be combined with the management of organic waste. According to the Harvard School of Public Health, 40% of the food that is produced is not eaten, and 95% of that food ends up in landfills. The problem stems from the amount of resources lost by wasting these products. The alternative, then, is to design these systems so that the gasification process uses solid biomass. The resulting fuel comes from sources that would otherwise be waste. This is intended to help the energy transition proceed in a way that keeps conventional technologies functional but without the negative impact they have today.

6a226c484b54f546d8876720.title: Smart Cities
6a226c484b54f546d8876720.subtitle: A sustainable proposal
6a226c484b54f546d8876720.body:
The percentage of Mexico's population living in urban areas has grown steadily in recent years. According to INEGI, the share of the population living in urban areas rose from 43% in 1950 to 79% in 2020.
The concentration of human activity in a relatively small area leads to climate problems, administrative problems, problems with the availability and distribution of resources, crime, and many others. For this reason, in 2015 the United Nations emphasized the need to address this problem by including it in its Sustainable Development Goals. Even so, the trend remains a migration from rural areas to cities, which worsens the problem. Smart cities are an innovative proposal that aims to maximize the advantages of modern information technologies to improve the administration of cities and the well-being of their citizens. The smart city proposal seeks to take advantage of an infrastructure based on information technologies to design and deploy solutions to problems caused by uncontrolled urbanization. Some of the technologies most commonly used to build this infrastructure are the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing, and sensors, among many others. These technologies can be used to implement solutions ranging from smart parking, which helps citizens find parking spaces, to dashboards that allow predictive analysis of crime patterns in the city. It is important to understand that the value of this idea lies not in how innovative the technologies are or in technological progress itself, but in knowing how to use them to create solutions that improve citizens' well-being and the progress of the community. One of the challenges to consider with this idea is the amount of sensitive information that will be handled. Skepticism and distrust toward large technology companies, and toward how they use the information they collect from their users, grow every day. Collecting data to manage a city can potentially leave its citizens in a vulnerable position, so it is essential to develop protocols and mechanisms that protect citizens and guarantee a level of anonymity within the infrastructure. Migration from rural areas to cities is projected to continue in the immediate future. The uncontrolled growth of cities, the emergence of new megacities, and all the associated challenges are now a problem we have seen coming. Although the smart city proposal has not been fully implemented in any city in the country, there are already examples of it in other countries such as China and the United States, where 
very favorable results have been observed.

6a226c484b54f546d8876722.title: Excessive Use of Plastics in Agriculture and Its Side Effects
6a226c484b54f546d8876722.subtitle: Impacts on health, soil integrity, and food production
6a226c484b54f546d8876722.body:
Agriculture is the most important primary economic activity in human history, and as a result ever more farmland has been developed to obtain better and greater quantities of food to supply human consumption. However, doing so involves using large amounts of plastic that are accumulating in soils, which can have “high repercussions for soil health, biodiversity and productivity, all of which are vital for human health,” says Professor Elaine Parker.
Plastics are present in many aspects of agriculture, both as macroplastics and as microplastics. The former can be found in protective wraps, greenhouse covers, irrigation pipes, and sacks; as they break down, they leach into the soil.
On the other hand, microplastics added as coatings on fertilizers and insecticides can change the physical structure of the soil and limit its ability to retain water, which affects the growth of plant roots and therefore reduces nutrient uptake.
All of this affects human health, because the side effects that occur in plants are passed on to people when they eat the products.
This situation is a concern for the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), which is why alternatives are being sought to improve the biodegradability of the polymers used, since current bio-based polymers are not 100% biodegradable and their price is a major problem.
That is why experts are calling for work on producing bio-based polymers that take into account the needs of sustainable agriculture; or else they urge growers to change the type of crop they plant so that less demand is placed on biopolymers, such as with cover crops.
In this way, with action both on developing new biodegradable polymers and on changing farming styles, this problem can be considerably reduced, making agriculture sustainable.

6a226c484b54f546d887672e.title: The Renewable Energy Market, Focusing on Solar Power
6a226c484b54f546d887672e.subtitle: How to lower your electricity consumption and be more sustainable with solar panels
6a226c484b54f546d887672e.body:
Electricity is essential today for any activity, whether working, studying, pursuing hobbies, or anything else. However, generating it releases large amounts of greenhouse gas emissions, since most of it comes from burning fossil fuels such as natural gas and fuel oil (CONAHCYT, 2023). The solution that has emerged is clean energy: energy sources and electricity generation processes whose emissions are below permitted thresholds or zero because they come from renewable sources such as the sun (photovoltaic), wind, water (hydroelectric), and biomass, and do not use fossil fuels (DOF, 2014).

Today, the technology that has grown the most in the energy market is solar panels, because they draw on an abundant source, solar radiation; they are highly adaptable, meaning they can be used in industry, businesses, or the home; and they are readily available, since they can be acquired more easily than other technologies (BBVA, 2022).

For this reason, installing them at home means savings on electricity costs (by reducing demand on the grid), lower emissions through efficient use of natural resources, and less dependence on fossil fuels. In addition, given Mexico's climate conditions, more than 70% of the national territory has potential for their installation, making it profitable for users given the low production cost and savings of up to 100,000 pesos per household (IMCO, 2019).

Solar panels are a more sustainable way to generate electricity that makes use of renewable natural resources such as sunlight, reducing dependence on the electric grid and, as a result, lowering household energy costs.

6a226c484b54f546d8876726.title: Success Stories - Sustainable Ventures
6a226c484b54f546d8876726.subtitle: México 10: ten sustainable entrepreneurs
6a226c484b54f546d8876726.body:
The main interest and motivation of today's entrepreneurs is to come up with an idea that helps solve social and environmental problems. Sustainable ventures emerge from this drive, developing alternatives that can meet present needs without compromising future generations. 

With this in mind, on November 15, Tecnológico de Monterrey, Disruptivo.tv, and Editorial LID, with the support of Tetra Pak, presented the book México 10: Emprendedores Sustentables at INCmty, the most important entrepreneurship festival in Latin America. As its name says, the book tells the stories of 10 successful Mexican ventures that seek to leave a positive impact on their surroundings, from clean energy generation to recycling and environmentally friendly products, among other things. 

One of the success stories featured is Ecolana, a Mexican company that promotes a culture of recycling and encourages responsible consumption of all kinds of products. The story of this project shows that you do not necessarily need years of preparation or to be an expert in entrepreneurship to take action and create a business that helps the environment and society. It all begins when Lisseth Cordero and Alejandra Valdez, two people passionate about recycling, realize that no one in Mexico was informing the public about how they can reuse and recycle their waste. Although there were many players in the recycling system, there was no connection among them, they were not up to date, and it was hard for people to reach collection centers.  

Like any venture, there were various challenges to face throughout the process, but it has all been worth it: Ecolana has now become one of the leading companies promoting recycling, with a presence across the country through different programs, and it aims to expand throughout Latin America. So far it has 16 employees, has reached more than 300,000 residents, and has recycled around 4,500 tons of waste.

Stories like this make us realize that more and more people and companies are becoming agents of change. And besides these examples, there are others that perhaps have not yet reached the market or are not as well known, but each of them seeks to create a positive relationship among the economic, social, and environmental dimensions. 

You could be the next sustainable entrepreneur. Just remember that true sustainability in entrepreneurship means real involvement in all processes, including relationships with third parties and the environment, and promotes prosperity and greater social well-being, because the idea is to grow together and become a fairer and more equitable community.

6a226c484b54f546d8876729.title: The Impact of Gold Mining in Mexico
6a226c484b54f546d8876729.subtitle: The background of gold mining
6a226c484b54f546d8876729.body:
Mining and metal production is one of the economic sectors whose environmental impact is entirely disproportionate, owing to the impact of extraction and processing. In everyday life, people look at everything around them without being aware of all the processes that required exploiting a natural resource. Mining processes are a major area of opportunity for the industry when it comes to circular economy processes. According to Statista, Mexico is among the world's largest gold producers, ranking as the seventh largest, behind Ghana. Besides being a major gold producer worldwide, within its local economy 31.2% of the mining that takes place in Mexico comes from gold mines, with Sonora and Zacatecas as the main producing states.

Regarding the environmental impact of these practices, the consumption and alteration of water resources occur as the water table is altered and groundwater is displaced. Surface water and groundwater become contaminated with mineral salts, sulfates, nitrates, oxides, oils, greases, lubricants, chemicals, explosives, and heavy metals (arsenic, lead, cadmium, chromium, cyanide, and mercury). Tailings and tailings dams store pollutants; some evaporate and are absorbed by foliage, trees, and plants, some runs off into rivers or streams or seeps into the subsoil, contaminating water and wells, and some remains trapped in the dam. Seepage, spills, or leaks of contaminated water occur. The enormous extraction of water causes massive desertification, droughts, and the depletion of water sources. There is no mine that does not contaminate water. It is unavoidable in a mine and leaves the water unfit for human consumption or for agriculture. It is impossible to leave it in the same state in which it was found. 

Although the industry's production processes have difficulty transitioning to circularity, it is not impossible: research leads to ideation, which leads to the development of projects that eventually yield positive results for developing alternatives to what we have today. In the case of gold, the process has a potentially high environmental impact and many areas of opportunity, but having them means there is room for improvement. Moving toward these alternatives is gradually becoming a necessity in an economy whose top priority is to leave linear processes behind and achieve circular ones.

6a226c484b54f546d887672a.title: Beyond Recycling, Reusing and Reducing
6a226c484b54f546d887672a.subtitle: The R's of the Circular Economy
6a226c484b54f546d887672a.body:
You surely know the famous 3 R's rule. Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle are three concepts that emerged from the need to inform the public about actions that can reduce the environmental impact of the waste we generate, since we live in an age of mass consumerism in which things are replaced immediately and the old ones thrown away, without any awareness of the consequences for the environment.

Over time, proposals for more R's were added, aligned with changing society's consumption habits in order to reduce waste. That is why today we can find 3 R's, 7 R's, 9 R's, even 10 R's. According to Christopher Brosse in his book “La Basura No Existe: Hacia el suprarreciclaje y la Economía Circular,” however, there are endless possibilities in the Circular Economy for listing R's, because they refer to both tangible and intangible processes.

The Circular Economy is a concept made up of multiple processes that aim for materials to circulate indefinitely, whether from one product to another or from one process to another, always with the goal that they never become unused materials. Likewise, the Circular Economy aims to optimize the production of goods and services.

Some R's of the Circular Economy are the following:
Rethink the entire cycle of material use and the interaction consumers have with what is produced.
Reduce our consumption, bearing in mind that our individual actions always have consequences.
Remanufacture in order to make use of the materials in products whose useful life has ended because of a defect.
Reuse products to extend their useful life as much as possible.
Recycle things that have already been used so they can be used again.
Redesign products to make their recycling more efficient and extend their useful life.
Repair items before buying new ones.
Renovate products in order to give them a new use or aesthetic appearance.
Recover materials and products to use them again.
Refuse what we do not need.

6a226c484b54f546d8876731.title: The Impact of Film on the Environment
6a226c484b54f546d8876731.subtitle: Green film shoots
6a226c484b54f546d8876731.body:
Film is a very large and vast industry in which producing a movie uses large quantities of materials and resources, often treated as if they were unlimited.
Consider just the materials used to dress each scene of any film: wood, plastic, and others can become unusable after their main use and are thrown away immediately. The same happens with makeup materials for visual effects and with a production's wardrobe and costumes.
For a broader picture, it is worth noting that keeping a crew on a production is also quite costly, since a crew of this kind involves anywhere from 50 to 500 people who need food and water, as well as a building with good lighting and a pleasant environment that also requires maintenance.
It is estimated that around 700 films and 500 series are made in the United States alone, and the estimated carbon dioxide emitted per year is 15 million tons.
Some companies are already working to reduce this impact on the environment. They seek to optimize production with certain strategies, from planning a film with a script that requires fewer materials, to using materials that can be reused or recycled, to powering the building with renewable energy, or even something as simple as replacing water bottles for the cast and staff with reusable or biodegradable ones.
A good example of this was the production of the film Spider-Man 2, which was recognized for having an eco-friendly strategy in its making.
Besides entertaining us, film gives us different perspectives on problems that are unfolding today. Just as films leave us with a lesson so that we can implement measures to protect the environment, the film industry needs to keep up this sense of concern and continue planning strategies to reduce its environmental impact.

6a226c484b54f546d8876728.title: Consumerism and Its Effects on Climate Change
6a226c484b54f546d8876728.subtitle: Do we consume out of need or because we want to?
6a226c484b54f546d8876728.body:
Consumerism is the uncontrolled tendency to acquire goods and services that are not always necessary for human beings. This practice often has consequences that many of us do not see, such as the excessive production of goods to satisfy the demand society generates. All of this also causes the overexploitation of soil, water, air, and other resources, along with the depletion of natural resources. These activities are responsible for 60% of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Much of what we consume contains plastic, and plastic contributes to the emission of these gases from its production (through fossil fuels), manufacture, and transport to its final disposal. Once it becomes waste, it emits methane and ethylene after being exposed to sun, air, or water. Despite this, around 380 million tons of plastic continue to be produced for its many uses.

That is why we must avoid consumerist practices and truly ask ourselves whether we need what we are about to consume or are simply buying for the sake of buying. Large companies encourage this behavior because it means greater financial gain for them, regardless of the consequences, and they often make it look as though they are taking action to help with climate change when in reality they are not.

6a226c484b54f546d887672d.title: Torre Reforma: A “LEED’er” in Environmental Design
6a226c484b54f546d887672d.subtitle: LEED certification is changing the way we build the buildings of the future.
6a226c484b54f546d887672d.body:
Torre Reforma is located in Mexico City, on Paseo de la Reforma avenue. The building was designed by architect Benjamín Romano and his firm LBR & A. After it was built, it won the award for best skyscraper in the world in 2018 at the International Highrise Award. 
Why do we call it a “LEED’er” in sustainability?
Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design certification, known as LEED, is a system that certifies new buildings and measures their level of sustainability in different areas, such as:
-Location and transportation. Does it encourage the use of public transport or bicycles?
-Water efficiency. Is water used to the fullest?
-Innovation. Are better techniques used?
-Energy and atmosphere. Is energy use optimal?
-Sustainable sites. How does it impact external factors, such as flora and fauna?
-Materials and resources. Where do the construction materials come from? Are they recycled?
-Indoor environmental quality. Are strategies used to promote good indoor ventilation?
-Regional priority. Were regional materials used to avoid long-distance transport?
Each category awards a certain number of points on a scale of 100. In turn, the certification has several levels depending on the score obtained: basic certification, silver, gold, and finally platinum, the last of which is the hardest to obtain, requiring 80 points or more.
Torre Reforma holds LEED Platinum certification, and thanks to it the building is now a benchmark in the industry and a symbol of sustainability. Among its notable features is that during construction the existing building was not demolished, and even its facade was preserved. The building also has Tetris-shaped openings on its sides, strategically placed to promote natural ventilation, improving airflow and reducing the use of air conditioning. Some of the meeting rooms are connected to terraces, so the doors can be opened to let air circulate, which also contributes to excellent ventilation. Finally, large windows and glass doors allow natural light to be used as the light source throughout the day. 
Currently, there are 509 buildings in Mexico with this certification, of which only 50 have platinum certification. Beyond being seen as awards, these new frameworks are essential for making sound, informed decisions when developing projects, whether in architecture, design, or any other field.

6a226c484b54f546d8876727.title: The Oceans and Life
6a226c484b54f546d8876727.subtitle: Are we aware of how important the oceans are in our lives?
6a226c484b54f546d8876727.body:
The oceans cover more than 90% of the planet's living space and are home to more than 250,000 marine species, and more than two thirds of them have yet to be discovered. The biodiversity of seas and oceans is vast, and we often fail to grasp how important these natural bodies are in our lives. It is very important to know what they give us and how vital it is to take care of them. Many of us believe that forests and jungles are the main suppliers of oxygen, but we are wrong: the sea produces more than half of the oxygen we breathe, and it absorbs about 26% of the carbon dioxide emissions released into the atmosphere.

Sadly, every year we begin to see phenomena that indicate these immense bodies of water are being harmed. Recently there has been an increase in sargassum on beaches because of the climate change we are living through. Likewise, we see more and more garbage, and tons of plastic reach these bodies of water. It is estimated that about 13 million tons end up in the sea. All this kind of garbage causes the death of 100,000 marine species. In addition, we have activities such as overfishing and habitat destruction, ecosystem pressure, and biodiversity loss. Excessive fishing, or overfishing, is not at all sustainable; it has led to about 60% of fish stocks being fully exploited and another 30% being fished at unsustainable levels, day after day.

That is why we should help take care of our planet; not littering the streets, rivers, and seas is a great help. Everything adds up, from saving energy to reducing our waste and contributing to actions for the planet. We must start eliminating the bad habits we have, one example being excessive consumption. This is the cause of much of what we see today as pollutants: overproduction generates a lot of waste that has nowhere to go and ends up flowing into the seas. If each of us changes these bad habits, we will begin to see improvements in the sea and thus have a greener planet.

6a226c484b54f546d887671f.title:
Improper Waste Management Has Environmental 
Impacts
6a226c484b54f546d887671f.subtitle: Consequences and how I can contribute from my home
6a226c484b54f546d887671f.body:
Climate change and global warming are a major problem today, and all of us
contribute to it. It causes 
the degradation of the environment and limits the amount of carbon that the earth is able to hold.
One of the many causes of this climate change is the exponential growth in waste generation 
in recent years: when large amounts of it accumulate and are poorly managed, 
they become a source of greenhouse gases. In addition, waste can harm 
health, in the form of disease, and it can also have harmful effects on the 
environment: on the aesthetics of cities, on natural landscapes and their species, and through 
pollution of water, soil and air, which affects our quality of life.
What consequences can poor waste management have?
1) Air pollution: The accumulation of large amounts of waste in one area can
lead to slow decomposition with little or no oxygen. Bad 
odors and polluting gases are also released.
2) Water pollution: When there is no waterproof layer to protect and insulate the 
soil, the leachate from the decomposition and compression of waste 
seeps or filters through the soil. It can reach groundwater aquifers, 
polluting the water, and rivers carry waste along and deposit it in lakes and 
oceans.
3) Soil degradation: Waste from different sources accumulates, combines and 
alters the physical and chemical properties of the soil. This alteration reduces its 
fertility, aeration capacity, water retention and porosity. Improperly accumulating 
waste in unauthorized areas can also increase the risk of fires.
4) Disruption of ecosystems: The carrying capacity and regenerative capacity of the ecosystem are 
exceeded by uncontrolled waste accumulation. Habitats and the species 
that make them up are affected. An example is the waste that is carried off by marine currents and 
spread out, and much of which settles on the seabed, affecting life and 
food chains.
How can I help reduce waste from my home?
1. Reduce food waste. When we throw food in the trash, we are also 
wasting the energy and water used for production, transport, 
storage and waste management.
2. Sort and recycle. Separate plastic containers, paper and cardboard, glass, organic 
matter and the remainder, and put them in the right bin.
3. Avoid plastic bags. If you bring your own cloth or raffia bag when you shop, you avoid 
being given a new one each time.
4. Make home compost. Use your organic waste to make your own compost 
and produce natural fertilizer.
5. Cut down on disposable products. Use products that are reusable or 
refillable to give them more lives.
It is important to review our daily actions and think about how we can reduce 
our impact on the climate and improve how we manage waste at home.

6a226c484b54f546d887672b.title: MDF: The Disguised Material
6a226c484b54f546d887672b.subtitle: A Sustainable Scam
6a226c484b54f546d887672b.body:
We should begin by asking ourselves: what is MDF?
It is known by its English initials, Medium Density Fibreboard, which means it is a medium-density fiber material. It is made from solid wood fibers, often recycled, which means we are talking about a recycled material that is highly sustainable. This material has the advantage that it does not warp with humidity the way solid wood does, although it is still not advisable to leave it exposed in places where humidity is very high. Another benefit is that, because it is made of fiber, its surface is soft and smooth, making it easier to paint than solid wood, whose grain tends to show through. But this quality also works against it, because if MDF is scratched and/or cracked, it cannot be repaired.
Lastly, what seems to be MDF's biggest advantage is its price. This material is much cheaper than solid wood, and because it is manufactured by people rather than grown as a tree, it can be produced in larger boards. The affordable price makes it possible to create products that are more accessible to the general public.
Now, why is it said to be a disguised material?
Like other materials, MDF can be veneered, meaning it is covered with another material, such as a wood veneer or even melamine resins (which, incidentally, can protect MDF from humidity). These veneers initially allow the material to take on different finishes by giving the MDF another appearance, making it more versatile and, according to some, more beautiful.
The problem is that there have been cases of veneered MDF furniture and other products being sold as solid wood pieces, which means the price is greatly inflated. Sometimes the veneering work is so good that people with no knowledge of these materials fall for the scam.
 How can you identify a "disguised" MDF?
MDF that has been veneered with melamine is covered only on its length and width, that is, the thickness is left exposed. To hide this, there is a gummed strip, like a tape, with adhesive on one side and wood veneer or melamine on the other; this product is better known as edge banding. The trick is to look at the thickness of the material, where you can usually see a line separating the veneer from the edge banding. For wood veneer it is easier, because the way the grain of solid wood is distributed across a plank is different from what you see with edge banding. This can also be used together with the previous method.

6a226c484b54f546d887672f.title: From Invention to Environmental Crisis: The History of CFCs and the Ozone Layer
6a226c484b54f546d887672f.subtitle: The Ozone Hole
6a226c484b54f546d887672f.body:
Rowland, a professor of chemistry at the University of California, Irvine, and Molina, a postdoctoral fellow in Rowland's laboratory, had shown that chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) could destroy ozone, a molecule made of three oxygen atoms (O3), in the Earth's stratosphere. That stratospheric ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation that would otherwise reach the Earth's surface. At that time, CFCs were used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays. These compounds are inert and essentially nontoxic, characteristics that make them suitable for these applications. However, those same characteristics also made them a danger to life on Earth. Rowland, a professor of chemistry at the University of California, Irvine, and Molina, a postdoctoral fellow in Rowland's laboratory, had shown that chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) could destroy ozone, a molecule made of three oxygen atoms (O3), in the Earth's stratosphere. That stratospheric ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation that would otherwise reach the Earth's surface. At that time, CFCs were used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays. These compounds are inert and essentially nontoxic, characteristics that make them suitable for these applications. However, those same characteristics also made them a danger to life on Earth.

In the 1920s, refrigeration and air-conditioning systems used toxic and flammable compounds as refrigerants. Thomas Midgley Jr. and his team developed nontoxic alternatives, such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which became popular and led to mass production by the 1970s.

However, in the 1970s, scientists such as F. Sherwood Rowland and Mario J. Molina discovered that CFCs released into the atmosphere destroyed the stratospheric ozone layer, which is crucial for protecting against harmful ultraviolet radiation. This sparked concerns about health and the environment.

Despite the initial controversy, compelling evidence, including the discovery of the hole in the ozone layer over Antarctica in 1985, led to the signing of the Montreal Protocol in 1987, an international agreement to reduce and gradually eliminate the production of CFCs and other substances harmful to the ozone layer.

This episode shows how scientific research and international action can address global environmental problems, and it highlights the importance of protecting the ozone layer as a precedent for tackling climate change.

6a226c484b54f546d8876732.title: The Bhopal Industrial Catastrophe: The Lasting Legacy of a Deadly Leak
6a226c484b54f546d8876732.subtitle: The Union Carbide Disaster in India and Its Lasting Impact on Health and the Environment
6a226c484b54f546d8876732.body:
A leak of methyl isocyanate from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, caused more than 7,000 deaths and thousands of injuries, and 35 years later it continues to harm the population. In the early hours of December 3, 1984, a toxic cloud engulfed the city of Bhopal, in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India. The pesticide plant of the American company Union Carbide let escape methyl isocyanate (MIC), an extremely toxic gas used to make insecticides. The accident was caused by a pressure increase in the storage tank, which made the safety valve open and release the gas into the atmosphere. The plant's safety systems, such as the gas scrubber and the flare tower, failed to prevent the tragedy.

More than 7,000 people died; many were asleep at that hour and had no time to escape. Hundreds of domestic, wild and commercial animals also died, and water wells were contaminated, harming the families who drank from them.

Methyl isocyanate is a substance that can be absorbed through inhalation and through the skin; it attacks the respiratory and circulatory systems, with symptoms similar to those of an asthma attack. Continued inhalation for a few minutes causes death by chemical burns to the lungs and has mutagenic effects. Many people went blind or lost their sense of smell, hearing or touch. Others succumbed to secondary neurological, immunological and carcinogenic effects. Pregnant women had miscarriages, and others who gave birth in the following months had children with congenital malformations. It also caused genetic and hormonal damage in people.

Even now, 35 years after the accident, the population suffers its serious aftereffects: children are born with physical and mental disabilities, blind and deaf, with chronic illnesses, respiratory problems, blindness, cancers and hormonal disorders.

6a226c484b54f546d8876733.title: Waste in the Health Sector
6a226c484b54f546d8876733.subtitle: Healthcare waste and its impact on the environment
6a226c484b54f546d8876733.body:
Waste management in the health sector is an important issue that must be recognized and seen at scale. In developed countries, an average of half a kilogram of hazardous waste is produced per hospital bed, while in less developed countries this figure is 0.2 kg (WHO, 2018). However, because these countries still lack adequate healthcare waste management, the figure rises considerably.
First, separating the different types of waste in places that provide health care to a population is essential to avoid greater risks for the general public, since this waste can trigger infections and physical harm. It can come from hospitals, health centers, clinics, laboratories and even research centers (Méndez, 2012).
On the other hand, general waste that poses no risk to the population, which accounts for 85% of a hospital's total waste, is commonly incinerated in developing countries. This can cause significant damage to the environment, as various pollutants are released that would affect the atmosphere, with carcinogenic potential (WHO, 2018). 
It can even happen that hazardous waste previously used, such as syringes, is reused after being discarded, posing an enormous health risk to the people in charge of handling this waste (Salud sin Daño, 2023). Preventing the general population from being exposed to it is essential.
It is important to take note of this kind of practice, especially in hospitals in developing countries or in communities without the capacity to handle this waste, in order to develop different strategies focused on its proper treatment. 
Measures must be learned and implemented, such as selecting appropriate methods that reduce health risks throughout the processing of this waste, as well as spreading this knowledge to different health centers regardless of their size.

6a226c484b54f546d887671d.title: Energy Efficiency
6a226c484b54f546d887671d.subtitle: The cleanest energy is the energy you don't use.
6a226c484b54f546d887671d.body:
The main topic of conversation when discussing sustainable development is the technologies that can be used to supply the processes that require energy without causing the harm that fossil-fuel technologies do. However, the fact that the cleanest energy is the energy that is not used is often ignored. Graph 1 shows that every energy source involves a certain number of tons of CO2 associated with its production. According to the World Nuclear Association, there is not a single energy process whose nature allows it to be harmless or beneficial to the environment.
So the challenge in the energy sector is to reduce the impact associated with it. How? In large part, by reducing the consumption tied to fossil-fuel operations, replacing them with renewable energy technologies. However, practices to reduce energy consumption are also needed. Energy efficiency practices are the key to making sure energy processes not only draw on clean sources, but also make the most of the energy so that none is wasted at any stage. Within itself, energy efficiency can be considered in terms of designing efficient processes, such as designing turbines, boilers, compressors, panels and the other processes involved in energy generation. The other aspect considered is energy consumption, since wasteful consumption can be another determining factor in the impact of energy use. According to the International Energy Agency, in 2016 the world would have used 12% more energy had it not been for improvements in energy efficiency since 2000. That is why it is important to promote these areas of sustainable development. Of course, we have to think about ways to provide clean energy, but just as it is easier to mitigate than to remedy damage, it is more beneficial to save energy than to generate it cleanly. The task for engineers, researchers and others involved in proposals for applying technologies to fight climate change is therefore both simple and complex: working out how energy processes and uses can get the most out of themselves.

6a226c484b54f546d8876730.title: The Controversy over the Carbon Footprint
6a226c484b54f546d8876730.subtitle: How a marketing strategy changed the perspective on sustainability
6a226c484b54f546d8876730.body:
A term that has become popular in the last decade when talking about sustainability is the carbon footprint. The carbon footprint is an environmental indicator that measures the greenhouse gas emissions generated by human activities (Iberdrola, 2021).

The carbon footprint has made countless individuals aware of the relationship between human activities and their impact on the environment, and it makes it possible to evaluate strategies for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Consequently, the carbon footprint has taken on an important role in sustainability efforts and the fight against climate change, as reflected in the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, in Goal 13: Climate action (United Nations, 2023). 

Where does this term come from? Why is it so relevant? The concept of the carbon footprint emerged in the late twentieth century; however, the term became popular because the company BP (formerly known as British Petroleum) launched its "carbon footprint calculator" in 2004. The main aim of this calculator was to let individuals calculate their personal carbon footprint and discover how their lifestyle contributes to climate change. 

However, another aim of this marketing campaign was to steer sustainability efforts toward the individual level in order to divert attention from the fact that companies like BP produced around 4 million barrels of oil per day in 2005 (Kaufman, 2020).

Its marketing strategy commits "greenwashing" by conveying the notion that BP is an environmentally responsible company, even though it is part of one of the most polluting industries on the planet (Heatable, 2023).

Despite the controversial popularization of the term "carbon footprint," it is impossible to deny that it has helped strengthen a culture of responsible consumption, set goals to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, fight climate change, and encourage people, companies and organizations to prioritize sustainability.

6a226c484b54f546d8876735.title: Sustainable Biomaterials in the Health Sector
6a226c484b54f546d8876735.subtitle: Biodegradable polymers and their applications in medicine
6a226c484b54f546d8876735.body:
Because of today's growing environmental problems, international organizations are demanding that products and services be built on sustainable foundations. The goal is to reduce the impact of the waste generated and to lower the total carbon footprint of consuming utilities or using a service. As a result, in the health sector, biodegradable polymers have gained relevance as an innovation to combat this environmental problem.
 This material seeks to replace disposable plastics and other compounds so that, at the end of their useful life as medical devices or implants, they can be degraded naturally by the body itself or disposed of without a major impact on the environment. This degradation process is possible because their structures can break down into smaller chemical fragments, which are finally absorbed by the body without leaving hazardous residues (Kunduru et al., 2016).
 It is important to note how important it is to choose the right material for these biomaterials, because of their direct contact with the human body and the risk of being detected by the immune system or rejected by the body outright. For this, there are several criteria to consider when creating these biomaterials, such as being unable to provoke inflammatory responses, having a degradation time consistent with their useful life, and degrading in a non-toxic way, among other important factors (Ulery et al., 2011).
 These materials already have several relevant medical applications, such as making containers, medical instruments, sutures, dressings, gauze, catheters, implants and even external prostheses (Oliver, 2021). In general, this area of research, which is related to tissue engineering, is extremely relevant to the development of the medical field and its important relationship with sustainability.

6a226c484b54f546d887671c.title: Learning About Climate Change
6a226c484b54f546d887671c.subtitle: Do we understand what climate change is?
6a226c484b54f546d887671c.body:
Climate change is one of the most talked-about topics in recent years, but do we really understand it? Do we know what causes it? Are we aware of its effects? In this article we will give you a brief explanation so that you can understand everything about climate change.

The world is surrounded by an atmosphere containing greenhouse gases (GHGs). These gases help keep the sun's heat inside the Earth, and that is what makes life possible. However, since the first Industrial Revolution, humans have been emitting these GHGs excessively: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and others.

GHG emissions have been rising steadily for years, so the heat trapped by the atmosphere keeps growing. This is how the Earth's average temperature has risen by 1°C since the First Industrial Revolution. It may seem like a small number, but the consequences of this change are enormous.

Even though we know that greenhouse gas emissions are the cause of climate change, we have not stopped producing them because they are closely tied to everything we do day to day: electricity, using a motorized means of transport, industrial production, food production, waste disposal, and so on. To reduce them, we must change how we consume, produce and dispose of things.

The consequences of climate change differ from region to region, and less developed countries will be the most affected. Some of the events that will intensify because of climate change are droughts, floods, fires and sea level rise, among others. As a result, there will be major challenges in food production and access to water, and climate migration will increase, among other effects.

Because of the magnitude of the problem, the world is acting together. In 2015 the Paris Agreement was signed, in which the world's countries committed to taking action so that the rise in global average temperature does not exceed 2°C, while making efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. 

The plans to confront climate change include mitigation and adaptation strategies. The first, mitigation, refers to actions that help reduce the amount of greenhouse gases reaching the atmosphere. The second, adaptation, refers to the measures that will be taken in response to the already unavoidable effects of climate change in order to reduce their impact.

Climate change is an enormous and quite complex problem, so solutions are needed from every sector if we are to guarantee a habitable planet. The first step is to inform ourselves so that we can act intelligently and quickly. It is important that we start acting today, to take care of our tomorrow.

6a226c484b54f546d8876721.title: Unsustainable Consumption
6a226c484b54f546d8876721.subtitle: Sustainability in a disposable world
6a226c484b54f546d8876721.body:
Rapid urban growth, overpopulation and various cultural, social, family and personal factors have brought society to a point of overproduction and overconsumption of goods, both necessary and unnecessary and of all kinds, from technology to food. This situation directly affects the environment and natural resources, to the point that Goal 12, Responsible Consumption and Production, was defined as one of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) developed by the United Nations (UN) as part of an agenda to end and improve the state of the world on a range of relevant topics.

According to UN estimates, one third of the food that is produced is wasted every year, either because an excessive amount was produced and ended up rotting or because it was not stored and transported properly. Likewise, future projections have determined that if the world population reaches 9.6 billion or more by 2050, the situation will become unsustainable, since the equivalent of at least three planet Earths would be needed to provide the resources for people to maintain a lifestyle similar to the one we know today.

To counteract the current situation and what is foreseen for the future, sustainable consumption and production are being promoted. They are based on the basic principle of doing more and better with less, that is, reducing the overexploitation of resources while maintaining, and even improving, the quality of goods and services by finding alternatives with a smaller ecological footprint. This would not only bring sustainability benefits by allowing ecosystems and natural resources to recover gradually, but would also bring social improvements, such as reducing poverty and social inequality. 

Specifically, to achieve this SDG, the UN defined a series of concrete targets, among which some stand out, such as encouraging governments and large companies to adopt sustainable practices and halving food waste, among others. Of these targets, it is important to stress the role of companies. While it is true that individual actions can have a massive collective impact (as the UN notes when it estimates that 120 billion dollars a year would be saved if all citizens used energy-efficient light bulbs), it is largely big corporations that have the greatest impact, for better or for worse, as in the case of Coca-Cola and the excessive amount of water it uses to produce its soft drink.

In conclusion, the collective lifestyle we are leading today is steering us toward an unsustainable future in which resources will not be enough to meet even the most basic needs. Although it is everyone's responsibility, and although it may not seem so, every individual action counts, it is true that pressure must be put on governments and organizations to opt for a style and process of resource efficiency in order to move to a fully sustainable model.

6a226c484b54f546d887671e.title: Life Cycle Assessment and Its Importance in Evaluating “Sustainable” Alternatives
6a226c484b54f546d887671e.subtitle: Stages of Life Cycle Assessment
6a226c484b54f546d887671e.body:
Because of awareness of climate change and its consequences, companies are working on "sustainable" alternatives to products with a very high environmental impact, mainly seen in single-use items. In advertising we find claims such as "Made with 100% recycled material," "Biodegradable packaging," "Made from natural fibers," and so on. This makes us, as consumers, ask ourselves: is it more sustainable to buy this product instead of the other one? Am I really making a difference? Which product pollutes less? 

Fortunately, there is a tool called Life Cycle Assessment that allows specialists to estimate the environmental impact of product processes.

What is Life Cycle Assessment?
Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is a methodology that makes it possible to objectively calculate and evaluate the environmental impacts that a product, process or activity can generate during all stages of its life. This tool makes it possible to:
●        Quantify the energy and materials used, as well as the waste released into the environment.
●        Evaluate the impact generated by the products used (energy and materials) and the emissions to the environment.
●        Identify the critical points of the processes in order to look for solutions that improve the process. 

Stages of LCA 
To carry out an LCA, the following stages must be followed: 
1.        Goal and scope definition: The goals describe the reasons the study is being carried out, the intended application and who it is addressed to. The scope sets out the stages of the product's life that will be considered, which can be:
●        Gate to Gate: Takes into account only the production process of the company that makes the product.
●        Cradle to Gate: Considered from the extraction of the raw material through the production process.
●        Gate to Grave: Considers the production process of the company that makes the product and extends through the waste management phase.
●        Cradle to Grave: Covers everything from obtaining raw materials to the final management of waste, whether recycling, reuse, and so on.
●        Cradle to Cradle: The product's entire life cycle is analyzed, that is, from the extraction of raw materials until the product is reintroduced into the same production process or another.
2.        Life Cycle Inventory (LCI): Includes the identification and quantification of the inputs and outputs of the production system. The following software can be used for this stage:
●        Bousted Consulting Database and Software
●        ECO-iT
●        EIO-LCA
●        GaBi
●        IDEMAT
●        SimaPro
●        Umberto
●        TRACI

3.        Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA): Using the results obtained from the LCI, the significance of the potential impacts generated by the inputs and outputs is evaluated.

6a226c484b54f546d8876734.title: World Wetlands Day: Celebrating and Preserving Vital Ecosystems
6a226c484b54f546d8876734.subtitle: A Look at the Importance of Wetlands and the Threats They Face
6a226c484b54f546d8876734.body:
On February 2, World Wetlands Day is celebrated to commemorate the adoption of the Ramsar Convention in 1971. This convention is unique in its focus on protecting wetlands as a matter of international importance. Wetlands, defined as areas of land covered by water that host diverse ecosystems, are crucial both for humanity and for the sustainable development of the planet.
 
 These ecosystems are diverse and can be freshwater, brackish or saltwater. Wetlands are characterized by being habitats for a great variety of animal and plant species. Waterbirds such as ibises and kingfishers find in wetlands a refuge for nesting and feeding, giving these environments a unique beauty and vitality.
 
 Despite their importance, wetlands face serious threats. Human activity and the negative effects of climate change have had a devastating impact. Since 1970, 81% of inland wetland species populations and 36% of coastal and marine species have declined because of overexploitation and the climate crisis.
 
 Wetlands play a crucial role in the sustainability of the planet. They provide essential foods such as rice and supply most of the world's fresh water. They also regulate the climate and hydrological regimes, reduce pollution and mitigate the risk of natural disasters, such as floods or droughts. In addition, wetlands store carbon, and peatlands, salt marshes and mangroves hold more carbon than forests.
 
 The current water crisis threatens life on Earth, as we use more water than nature can regenerate. This threat endangers the survival of wetlands, affecting thousands of species and millions of people who depend on these ecosystems.
 
 Since 1700, nearly 90% of wetlands have been lost, and they are disappearing three times faster than forests. The loss of these ecosystems could have devastating effects on humanity. It is therefore crucial to raise awareness of the importance of protecting these natural environments on World Wetlands Day and to promote their sustainable management in order to preserve biodiversity and ensure a sustainable future.

text.Recursos del pueblo: 20 fichas de c/u (a:
Town resources: 20 tokens of each (environmental, economic and social).

There are press exposés, which can cancel a victory point just earned. Each player may use one during the game.

There are 4 types of cards. Scenario cards present a problem related to sustainable development — place them in the center. Proposal cards suggest possible solutions to the scenario problems depending on their category — shuffle them into piles.

All players start with 5 cards and must keep that number throughout the game. If you use one, you must draw another.

In each round one player is the mayor and the others are secretaries. The mayor takes a scenario card and reads it.

The participants each propose a card as a solution to the scenario presented, and the mayor decides who wins the victory point. The first to reach ten victory points wins.

There is no perfect solution to the scenario cards. Any missing resources must be filled in with town resources if the values on each card placed on the scenario card are not met.

Resources: Orange = Economic | Green = Environmental | Blue = Social
text.Un reconocido grupo farmacéutico al que: A well-known pharmaceutical group that your community supported doubled its annual net profit thanks to health needs related to Covid-19. It has recently been proven that its production processes are causing damage to the environment.
text.Es de gran importancia promover la educa: It is very important to promote quality education and research on sustainable development, so that new strategies and solutions can be devised for this urgent problem of humanity. But the budget available for these purposes is very small.
text.Entre las especies de insectos comestibl: Among the species of edible insects are crickets (Acheta domesticus), black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens) and mealworms (Tenebrio molitor). Climate change is reducing these insect populations at an accelerated rate.
text.Tus pobladores son dueños de buques pesq: Your townspeople own fishing vessels, and you are running out of fish in a highly in-demand fishing region. A study confirms that you are putting a fishing chain at risk and threatening sea species. You need to find a solution that regulates and regenerates fishing without jeopardizing your region's economic capacity.
text.Una nueva plataforma informática masiva,: A new massive computing platform, the planetary computer, has been launched. It will gather billions of data points on nature and give conservation organizations new tools to quickly analyze that information as they rush to solve the world's biodiversity crisis. The only catch is that its cost is high.
text.Las plantas, animales y microorganismos: The plants, animals and microorganisms that are the basis of food production are in decline. If these critical species are lost, the situation will get even worse. Changes in land use, pollution and climate change are causing this loss of biodiversity.
text.Investigaciones recientes muestran que u: Recent research shows that a global weather phenomenon, which would normally keep ocean temperatures lower on the Great Barrier Reef, may not be enough to stop another mass coral bleaching next summer, according to the marine park's chief scientist.
text.Nuevas investigaciones confirman que el: New research confirms that the increase in resource consumption and polluting emissions resulting from economic growth directly affects biodiversity. Your community has seen the populations of various plant and animal species decline because of pollution.
text.Eres mujer y estás a punto de lanzar un: You are a woman and you are about to launch a program that will help reduce CO2 emissions. However, the person who has to approve it is a man, and he does not think it is right for a woman to be in charge of such an important initiative, even though he knows that today it is vital for raising climate awareness in every country and thus adding to a collective effort.
text.El creciente auge por el E-Commerce amen: The growing boom in e-commerce threatens to lead to negative scenarios because of the growing need to transport goods and the decline of local commerce.
text.Surge un sistema nacional de fijación de: A national carbon emissions pricing system emerges. This new system is an unfavorable scenario for your city, as an industrial area where 60% of jobs are generated by factories that emit that gas; but it undoubtedly brings benefits in environmental terms.
text.El hambre mundial está aumentando debido: Global hunger is rising because of all the climate changes, mainly droughts, which is causing levels of malnutrition. This problem not only affects people's health and wellbeing, but also slows progress in development areas such as education and employment.
text.Un nuevo impuesto a medios alternos de t: A new tax on alternative means of transport such as electric vehicles threatens to hold back the development of new transport strategies to reduce GHG emissions.
text.Perdimos la carrera. El cambio climático: We lost the race. Climate change has reached extreme limits and it is time to halt production around the world to achieve environmental recovery.
text.Implementaste un programa para incentiva: You implemented a program to encourage the use of electric cars, but now the energy consumption of your cities has increased. What will you do?
text.Desde la Revolución Industrial la acidez: Since the Industrial Revolution, the acidity of surface ocean waters has increased by 30%. The ocean has absorbed between 20% and 30% of total anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions in recent decades (7,200 to 10,800 million metric tons per year). You must restore your aquatic ecosystems and protection laws to lessen the impact of the consequences.
text.Implementaste un programa de rescate de: You implemented a program to rescue your beekeepers using information technologies, which helped reduce the loss of pollinators (bees). You need economic resources for its continuation.
text.Después de hacer una investigación, desa: After carrying out research, you developed a code on pesticide management, creating an integrated pest control that does not kill pollinators.
text.Tu antecesor prefirió basar sus decision: Your predecessor preferred to base his growth decisions on benefiting private interests over social ones. The latest environmental impact projects damage the environment and generate profits for only a few. Your population is stuck with the bill. But you propose a new strategy to support the social interests that had been neglected.
text.Te uniste a la declaración de la Convenc: You joined the declaration of the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species to protect migrating birds, and you are going to help create connectivity areas for migratory species.
text.Apoyas activamente como voluntario en la: You actively volunteer in the logistics of the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, which seeks to formally recognize the rights and roles of Indigenous Peoples and local communities in international environmental agreements and to radically rethink the approach to conservation.
text.Apoyaste un proyecto en Madagascar, el c: You supported a project in Madagascar, led by teenagers from the island, who have started an agricultural revolution, working to keep food production from destroying the island's rich rainforest.

text.Sabiendo la importancia que tienen las m: Knowing the importance of women in decision-making on climate change, a workshop program is opened to integrate gender into national climate policies, plans and actions. text.Los productos de menstruación en México: Menstrual products in Mexico generate around 210 thousand tons of waste and take between 500 and 800 years to degrade. text.Implementas un nuevo sistema de sectores: You implement a new system of traffic-free zones, encouraging the development of new public spaces in the city while promoting the use of public transport systems, reducing the concentration of GHGs produced.
text.Desarrollas una solución de reciclaje in: You develop an innovative recycling solution for the benefit of Indigenous people in the city. Many Indigenous people in the city could learn to benefit from it and at the same time would be making a contribution to addressing climate change.
text.Desarrollas un nuevo sistema para calcul: You develop a new system to calculate consumers' carbon footprint in real time. This makes it possible to set a weekly limit on goods purchased per citizen based on the guidelines, thus reducing GHG pollution and waste produced.
